segments.script: Your skeleton is not one material — it is two: flexible cartilage and rigid bone. Both are connective tissues, built for very different demands.
segments.video_prompt: Side-by-side 3D render: left shows translucent glassy hyaline cartilage with visible chondrocytes in lacunae; right shows compact bone cross-section with a glowing Haversian canal at the centre surrounded by concentric lamellae. Deep blue and amber colour scheme, precision 3D render style.

segments.script: Cartilage is avascular and aneural. Chondrocytes live in lacunae within chondrin matrix, covered by perichondrium. Hyaline: fine collagen, smooth, in trachea and articular surfaces. Calcified: calcium deposits, rock-hard, at epiphyseal ends. Fibro-cartilage: densest collagen, strongest, in intervertebral discs and pubic symphysis. Elastic: elastic fibres, flexible, in pinna and epiglottis. Bone is vascular — osteocytes in lacunae within ossein plus hydroxyapatite matrix. Formation: cartilaginous endochondral for long bones, membranous for flat skull bones, sesamoid for patella. Long bone: epiphysis (spongy, red marrow, blood production), diaphysis (compact, yellow marrow). Structural unit: Haversian osteon — Haversian canal with blood vessels, concentric lamellae, osteocytes in lacunae, canaliculi, and Volkmann's canals connecting osteons.
segments.video_prompt: Top panel: a 2x2 grid of cartilage histology images — hyaline (clear glassy matrix), calcified (opaque dense), fibro-cartilage (white dense fibres), elastic (yellow branching fibres). Each labelled with type and location. Bottom panel: 3D cinematic zoom from the epiphysis (spongy trabecular bone, red marrow fill) into the diaphysis (compact bone cortex), then into a single osteon — Haversian canal centre glows amber, concentric lamellae rings, osteocytes in lacunae, canaliculi branching. Clinical precision render, warm bone tones.
